label: Reset rises at D1 after unrewarded trials, more after two; tracks belief S1 good.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; belief_lo ;; (prev_reward == 0) + (tv("reward", -2) == 0) + (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) ;; (phase != D1) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_reward == 0)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 12 (high at GO, mid at D1, low at D2). Beyond timing, the dominant driver is omission of reward: at D1 it rises ~+0.17 when the previous trial was unrewarded and a further ~+0.10 when the trial before was also unrewarded. Across all phases it rises graded with the ideal observer log-odds that S1 is good (belief_lo), i.e. higher when S1/a1 is favoured. The free fit adds: a slow all-phase rise with the count of recent unrewarded trials (losing streaks keep the whole trial elevated), a stronger D1 unrewarded effect after an a1 choice, a dip at D1 after rewarded S1 outcomes, and a D2 boost when a1 was just chosen. Future reward, next choice and reversal timing add essentially nothing. Model outputs were not used.

issues: The 'more after two unrewarded trials' claim adds little. Dropping the tv('reward',-2) term only lowers test R^2 from 0.604 to 0.585, and putting prev_action==1 in its place scores 0.600.

belief_lo is the wrong shape and is wrongly applied to every phase. The D1 belief-decile residuals are not monotonic (they peak around deciles 4-6), while GO and D2 follow a sigmoid in belief. Switching belief_lo to (phase != D1)*belief and keeping the other two terms raises test R^2 from 0.552 to 0.651. With the raw belief probability, belief_lo's R^2 also falls when restricted to non-D1 phases (0.55).

The recorded short form leaves systematic errors. Misses show a phase-level bias: D1 is over-predicted by -0.046, and GO and D2 are under-predicted by +0.023. D1 after rewarded S1 outcomes is over-predicted (a2 S1 r -0.134, a1 S1 r -0.120). After a1 losses it is under-predicted (D2 after a1 S1 u +0.085, D1 after a1 S2 u +0.081).

At D1 the no-reward boost depends on belief. Raw residuals at D1 are a1 S2 u +0.325 and a1 S1 u +0.20, but a2 S1 u only +0.02. So unrewarded trials that leave S1 favoured raise the gate much more. The term (phase==D1)*(1-prev_reward)*belief captures this and raises test R^2 to 0.716. With that change the phase bias goes away (D1 -0.003, GO +0.001, D2 +0.001).

Residual misses with the better form: losing streaks keep every phase elevated, which shows up in the worst windows. D1 after a1 S2 r is under-predicted by +0.126. Adding a streak count term barely helps (0.717).
